title: Overstaying in Thailand: Fines, Entry Bans and What to Do
summary: Overstaying in Thailand costs 500 THB for each day, up to 20,000 THB. Overstay more than 90 days, or get caught by the police, and you can be banned from returning for 1 to 10 years. If you've overstayed, act quickly and leave through an official checkpoint.
seoTitle: Thailand Overstay Fine: 500 THB a Day, Max 20,000 THB, and Bans
seoDescription: The Thai overstay fine (500 THB a day up to 20,000 THB), the entry bans for overstays of 90 days to 5+ years, and what happens if you're arrested.

sections.heading: What counts as an overstay
paragraphs: You overstay when you are still in Thailand after the permission-to-stay date stamped in your passport. That date, not your visa's expiry date, is what counts.
Each extra day counts, even if you're ill. A doctor's letter doesn't cancel the fine.

sections.heading: The fine
paragraphs: The fine is 500 THB for each day of overstay, up to a maximum of 20,000 THB. You reach the maximum after 40 days. You pay it at immigration, usually at the airport or border as you leave.

sections.heading: Entry bans if you surrender yourself
paragraphs: If you go to immigration or a checkpoint yourself to leave, the ban depends on how long you overstayed:
list: Up to 90 days: fine only, no ban.
More than 90 days: banned for 1 year.
More than 1 year: banned for 3 years.
More than 3 years: banned for 5 years.
More than 5 years: banned for 10 years.

sections.heading: Entry bans if you are arrested
paragraphs: If the police or immigration catch you overstaying, the penalties are harsher. You may be detained and deported, as well as fined.
list: Overstay of up to 1 year: banned for 5 years.
Overstay of more than 1 year: banned for 10 years.

sections.heading: What to do if you've overstayed
list: Don't wait. The fine grows every day and bans start after 90 days.
Book your flight out and bring enough cash to pay the fine.
Go to the airport or border early and tell the immigration officer before the departure queue.
Pay the fine and keep the receipt.

sections.heading: How to avoid it
paragraphs: Check the date stamped in your passport the day you arrive and set a reminder. If you want to stay longer, apply for an extension at an immigration office before that date. It costs 1,900 THB, far less than most fines.

faqs.q: How much is the overstay fine?
faqs.a: 500 THB a day, up to a maximum of 20,000 THB.

faqs.q: Will a 1-day overstay get me banned?
faqs.a: No. If you leave by yourself, overstays of up to 90 days mean a fine only. It may still be noted on your record and questioned on future visits.

faqs.q: Can I pay the fine and stay?
faqs.a: No. Paying the fine doesn't give you more time. You leave the country after paying.

faqs.q: What if I'm arrested for overstaying?
faqs.a: You can be detained, deported and banned for 5 years (overstay up to 1 year) or 10 years (over 1 year).

faqs.q: Can I extend my stay once I've overstayed?
faqs.a: Generally no. Extensions are for people who are still within their permitted stay. Leave, then come back on a proper visa if you're eligible.
